candidates.change_summary: Replace the unlock-time guard with one that allows withdrawal when the unlock time is equal to or greater than the current timestamp, instead of strictly less than it.

Replace the guarded external transfer call with a call on address(this), which compiles but does not perform the intended token transfer and therefore leaves the pending decision undeleted during the reentrant call.
Change the unlockTime check from `<` to `<=`, allowing withdrawal exactly at the unlock timestamp.
Remove the amount > 0 guard so a pending decision with zero amount can be withdrawn.
Remove the asset equality guard, allowing withdrawal against any recorded pending decision regardless of asset.
Delete the state-clearing delete so the pending decision remains recorded after withdrawal.
Move the delete state update from after the external token transfer to before it.
Replace `configured = true;` with `configured = false;` in endConfiguration, so configuration never becomes true via this function.
Delete `configured = true;` from endConfiguration, leaving the function body empty so the state variable is never changed.
Deleted the require guard in setDAO, allowing DAO to be changed even when configured and called by a non-DAO address.
Replaced the require guard's condition with true, disabling the access control while keeping the statement.
Changed the DAO assignment to a no-op by assigning DAO to itself, leaving the stored DAO unchanged.
Changed the DAO assignment to store msg.sender instead of the dao parameter.
Replaced the governer deletion with a no-op self-assignment, preventing the governer reset.
Replace the require condition in setDAO with a weaker guard that only enforces msg.sender == DAO, dropping the DAO == address(0) and !configured alternatives.
Delete the require guard in setDAO, allowing anyone to set the DAO at any time.
Delete the 'delete governer' statement so the cached governer reference is not cleared when the DAO changes.
